items.title: With high probability there is no small separator whose complement has between u_1 and n/2 vertices
items.author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
items.work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement excludes small separators at the lower end of the window (author lemma at source lines 772-778, label lem:no-small-separator). The proof (source lines 780-797) is a two-case union bound whose inputs are the counting lemma for large sets with a small boundary and the expansion estimate: the large-boundary case is handled by a direct first-moment estimate reaching o(n^{-3}), and the small-boundary case by the counting lemma combined with the expansion estimate to reach exp(-alpha'_M b) (proof lines 787-795). The case split on the size of the edge boundary is what makes the estimate uniform in b. H2.
